args.message:
Fix FIN-212: use ROUND_HALF_EVEN (banker's rounding) in round_money

The docstring already specified banker's rounding per FIN-212, but the
implementation used ROUND_HALF_UP. Switch to ROUND_HALF_EVEN so
half-way values round to the nearest even cent (e.g. 2.665 -> 2.66),
matching tests/test_money.py.

args.head: fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding
args.title: Fix FIN-212: use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) in round_money
args.body:
The nightly build failed because `tests/test_money.py` expects banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212, but `src/money.py` was implemented with ROUND_HALF_UP.

**Change:** Switch `round_money` to use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, so half-way amounts round to the nearest even cent (e.g. `2.675 -> 2.68`, `2.665 -> 2.66`).

**Verification:** CI passed on commit 08d3cd5986, including `tests/test_money.py`.

trace.final:
Done. Summary:

- **Root cause:** `src/money.py` used `ROUND_HALF_UP` despite its docstring and the FIN-212 requirement specifying banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`), which broke `tests/test_money.py`.
- **Fix:** Created branch `fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding` and switched `round_money` to use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`.
- **CI:** Triggered a run on the branch (`ci-0001`) — it **passed**, including the banker's rounding tests.
- **PR:** Opened PR #101 against `main` (https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101) with alex requested as reviewer.

Since main is protected, merging will need code-owner approval — I've left that with alex.
